episode.action: cholera outbreak investigated; pump handle removed; cesspool percolation established

title.zh: 拆掉水泵把手，宽街的霍乱就停了吗？
title.en: Did Removing the Pump Handle Really Stop the Cholera in Broad Street?

dek.zh: 1854年伦敦宽街，一口公共水泵的把手被拆掉。提出建议的医生自己提醒：病例在那之前已经在下降。把证据链补上的，是一位本以为能推翻水泵说的牧师。
dek.en: In 1854 London, the handle of a public pump in Broad Street was taken off on a doctor's advice. The doctor himself warned that cases were already declining before then. The man who closed the gap in the chain of evidence was a clergyman who had set out to disprove the pump theory.

heading.en: Ten Days, Five Hundred Dead, One Well

paras.zh: 1854年8月31日起，伦敦宽街一带突然暴发霍乱。按斯诺的统计，剑桥街与宽街交汇处250码以内，十天里有五百多人因霍乱死亡；不到六天，灾情最重的几条街走空了四分之三以上的居民。教区的调查委员会事后把这几天称作“突然、猛烈而集中的暴发”。
paras.en: On 31 August 1854 cholera broke out with sudden violence in the Broad Street neighbourhood of London. By John Snow's tally, within two hundred and fifty yards of the point where Cambridge Street joins Broad Street there were upwards of five hundred fatal attacks in ten days, and in less than six days the worst-affected streets had been deserted by more than three-quarters of their inhabitants. The parish inquiry committee, looking back, described those days as a sudden, severe and concentrated outbreak that began on 31 August and lasted through the first few days of September.

paras.zh: 医生约翰·斯诺怀疑街角那口公共水泵。他拿不出能给人看的病原体，只有死亡名单和打听来的饮水情况：在这口泵供水的范围内，有61名死者据说常喝或偶尔喝宽街泵水，6例因亲友死的死、走的走而问不到，6例据说发病前不喝。
paras.en: The physician John Snow suspected the public pump on the street corner. He had no pathogen he could put in front of anyone, only lists of the dead and hearsay about what they drank: within the pump's catchment, sixty-one of the deceased were said to have drunk Broad Street pump-water constantly or occasionally; in six cases no information could be obtained, because everyone connected with the dead person had died or moved away; and in six cases the deceased were said not to have drunk the pump-water before falling ill.

paras.zh: 地点是伦敦威斯敏斯特的圣詹姆斯教区。能下令处置水泵的是教区济贫委员会，斯诺9月7日晚向它陈述情况，第二天把手就被拆下。教区另设霍乱调查委员会，成员包括两位教区执事、几位牧师和医生；名单注明，斯诺和怀特黑德牧师都是在最初任命之后增补的。
paras.en: The setting was the parish of St James's, Westminster. The body with authority over the pump was the parish Board of Guardians; Snow laid the circumstances before them on the evening of Thursday, 7 September, and the handle was removed the following day. The parish also appointed a Cholera Inquiry Committee — two churchwardens, clergymen and doctors; the list notes that Snow and the Revd. H. Whitehead were among those added after the committee was first appointed.

paras.zh: 当时还没有今天的细菌学说。斯诺只能说水里有“霍乱毒物”，它是什么、怎样致病，谁也拿不出实物。他甚至在给委员会的报告里写道，井水“并非不可能”因为某种原因已经不再含有霍乱毒物。
paras.en: There was no germ theory as we know it. Snow could only say the water contained "the cholera poison"; what it was, and how it caused illness, nobody could produce in physical form. He even wrote in his report to the committee that it was "not improbable that the water had, from some cause or other, ceased to contain the cholera poison"

paras.zh: 这片街区本身还压着一段旧账。1665至1666年大瘟疫期间，克雷文伯爵在这里先租后买下一块地，建起收容瘟疫病人的房子（据说有36间），并辟了埋葬成千死者的公共墓地，后来这里得名瘟疫地。1851年和1853至54年两次铺设新下水道，深沟穿过这块地的部分区域，工程于1854年2月完工。所以当时另有一种地方性解释要排除：是不是挖沟惊动了地下的古代瘟疫坑？委员会核查工程记录后写道，“没有证据显示”任何一条线路直接穿过古代瘟疫坑，开挖时没有出现严重公害，周围居民的健康也没有立即受累。
paras.en: The neighbourhood also carried an old debt of its own. During the Great Plague of 1665-66, the Earl of Craven first hired and then bought a field here, on which pesthouses (said to number thirty-six) were built for people struck by the disease, and where a common burial ground was made for thousands who died of it. The place became known as the plague field. In 1851 and again in the winter of 1853-54, deep cuttings for new sewers were driven through parts of this ground, the latter works finishing in February 1854. So one local explanation had to be ruled out: had the digging stirred up ancient plague pits underground? The committee examined the works records and wrote that "no evidence exists of either line having passed directly through an ancient plague-pit"; no serious nuisance occurred when the ground was opened, and no immediate ill consequences followed for the health of surrounding inhabitants.

heading.en: Start with the People Who Were Fine

paras.zh: 斯诺的查法是先看谁没事。波兰街济贫院四分之三以上被死过人的房子包围，535名在院者只有5人死于霍乱；院里有自己的泵井，还接了大联合水厂的水，从不去宽街取水。按紧邻它三面的街道的死亡率，这里本该死一百多人。宽街啤酒厂就在泵边，七十多名工人没有人重症，只有两人轻微不适；老板说工人有麦芽酒配给，他相信他们根本不喝水，厂里另有一口深井，还接了新河公司的水。
paras.en: Snow's method was to look first at who escaped. The workhouse in Poland Street was more than three-quarters surrounded by houses in which cholera deaths occurred, yet of five hundred and thirty-five inmates only five died of cholera, the other deaths being people admitted after they were already attacked. The workhouse had its own pump-well on the premises, in addition to water from the Grand Junction Waterworks, and the inmates never sent to Broad Street for water. Had mortality matched the streets around it on three sides, upwards of a hundred people would have died. There was a brewery in Broad Street, close by the pump, employing above seventy workmen, and not one of them suffered severely; only two were indisposed, and not seriously, while the disease prevailed. The proprietor, Mr. Huggins, said the men were allowed a certain quantity of malt liquor and he believed they did not drink water at all; he was quite certain they never obtained water from the street pump. The brewery had a deep well of its own, in addition to the New River water.

paras.zh: 同一条街上也有反面例子。宽街37号的雷管厂雇了约两百名工人，厂里两只桶总是装满街上那口泵的水，谁想喝就喝；结果18名工人在自己家中死于霍乱，16男2女。啤酒厂和雷管厂同在宽街，一个靠麦芽酒和自家深井，一个靠街上的泵水，结局差得很远。
paras.en: The same street also supplies the counterexample. At the percussion-cap manufactory at 37 Broad Street, where about two hundred workpeople were employed, two tubs stood on the premises always supplied with water from the street pump, for anyone who wished to drink; eighteen of those workers died of cholera at their own homes, sixteen men and two women. Brewery and manufactory were both on Broad Street. One drank malt liquor and deep-well water, the other drank the street pump-water, and the outcomes could hardly have differed more.

paras.zh: 最能说明问题的病例却不在宽街。住在汉普斯特德西区的E太太几个月没到过宽街一带，只是喜欢那口泵的水，每天有车从宽街出发，给她捎一大瓶。8月31日捎来的水，她当晚喝了，周五又喝，周五傍晚发病，周六去世。来看她的侄女也喝了这水，回到伊斯灵顿地势高、环境好的家中后发病身亡。斯诺注明，当时这两处都没有霍乱。
paras.en: Yet the most telling case lay nowhere near Broad Street. A Mrs. E, living at West End, Hampstead, had not been in the neighbourhood of Broad Street for many months; she simply preferred the pump's water, and a cart went out from Broad Street every day carrying a large bottle of it for her. The water was taken out on Thursday, 31 August; she drank of it that evening and again on Friday. She was seized with cholera on Friday evening and died on Saturday. A niece who was visiting drank the water as well, returned to her home in a high and healthy part of Islington, and was attacked and died. Snow noted that at the time there was no cholera at West End, or in the neighbourhood where the niece died.

paras.zh: 9月7日晚，斯诺向教区济贫委员会陈述了这些情况，第二天，水泵把手被拆下。但他自己的统计显示，疫情在那之前已经转弱：每天新发病例从143降到116，再到54；把手拆下的9月8日新发12例，9日11例，10日和11日各5例，12日只剩1例，此后单日再没超过4例。按这组数字，下降在拆把手之前就已经开始。
paras.en: On the evening of 7 September Snow put these facts to the parish Board of Guardians, and the pump handle came off the next day. But his own figures show the outbreak weakening before then: daily fresh attacks fell from one hundred and forty-three to one hundred and sixteen, then to fifty-four. On 8 September — the day the handle was removed — there were twelve attacks; on the 9th, eleven; on the 10th and 11th, five apiece; on the 12th, only one; and after that never more than four in a single day. On these figures the decline began before the handle came off.

paras.zh: 怀特黑德牧师起初并不相信。他后来写道，刚听说暴发被归咎于水泵时，他对一位医生朋友说，仔细调查会推翻这种说法；他也坚持把每个难解的病例查到底：“这个问题太重要，不能为了一套理论的整齐而牺牲。”转折发生在他为别的事翻阅登记署周报的时候：宽街40号一个五个月大的女婴，9月2日死亡，死前腹泻已四天。他认识这家人，却一直没问她何时发病，按他自己的说法，大概因为那只是个婴儿的病例，就轻轻放过了。他立刻上门，从孩子母亲那里得知：女婴8月28日发病，排泄物到8月30日停止；洗尿布的水，一部分倒进后院水槽，一部分倒进前院的化粪池。
paras.en: The Revd. H. Whitehead did not believe it at first. He later wrote that when he first heard of the outbreak being attributed to the pump, he told a medical friend "my belief that a careful investigation would disprove that theory", and he insisted on chasing every puzzling case to the bottom: "It is far too important a subject to be sacrificed to the symmetry of a theory." The turn came while he was reading the Registrar's Returns for an unrelated purpose and his eye fell on an entry: at 40 Broad Street, on 2nd September, a daughter aged five months, exhaustion after an attack of diarrhoea four days previous to death. He knew the case and had recorded the date of death, but had somehow neglected to ask when the illness began — he supposed he had passed over it lightly because it was an infant's case. Nor had it occurred to him that the child might have been ill all week. He went to the house at once and learned from the mother, who occupied the back parlour, that the child was attacked on Monday, 28 August, the dejections ceasing on Wednesday the 30th. Pressed further, she said the dejections were collected in napkins which were immediately steeped in pails, the water from which was poured partly into a sink in the backyard and partly into a cesspool in the front area.

paras.zh: 要紧的是位置：化粪池紧挨着泵井。怀特黑德马上报告委员会，委员会下令调查，由秘书和测量师执行，结果“清楚地确立了化粪池液体渗入井中这一总体事实”。一个本想推翻水泵说的人，找到了比暴发早几天发病的病例，并促成了这次检查。
paras.en: What mattered was the position: the cesspool sat right beside the pump well. Whitehead reported the facts to the Committee without delay, and they ordered an investigation, carried out by their Secretary and Surveyor, which "clearly established the general fact of percolation of fluid from the cesspool into the well". A man who had set out to disprove the pump theory had found a case that began days before the outbreak, and had prompted the inquiry that traced the route by which filth reached the water.

paras.zh: 委员会还正面比较了水与空气两种说法。有人会说，死者喝宽街的水只是巧合，因为这一带的人本来常喝它；委员会指出，这个巧合对空气说法更不利：宽街本身同样呼吸那里空气的人，大暴发期间只有十分之一死亡。
paras.en: The Committee also weighed the water hypothesis directly against the atmospheric one. If, it argued, the drinking of Broad Street water by those who died was a mere coincidence — what one would expect, since so many people in the neighbourhood, especially in Broad Street, constantly drank it — then that same coincidence bears far harder on any merely atmospheric theory: of those in Broad Street itself who breathed the air there during the great outbreak, only one in ten died.

paras.zh: 委员会在1855年发表的报告中一致认为，“霍乱区”内8月31日起那几天的暴发，“以某种方式归因于饮用该井的不洁之水”；至于水是怎样起作用的，委员会明确表示不支持任何一种假说，把机制问题留在了原地。
paras.en: In its report, published in 1855, the Committee concluded unanimously that the striking, disproportionate mortality in the "Cholera area" during the days from 31 August onwards "was in some manner attributable to the use of the impure water of the well". As for how the water acted, the Committee expressly declined to favour any hypothesis, leaving the question of mechanism exactly where it stood.

paras.zh: 这次调查有说服力，靠的不是拆把手，而是问法：不只问死者喝了什么，也看没喝的人怎么样。济贫院和啤酒厂离井很近，却几乎没人受害；雷管厂和E太太一近一远，却都喝了那口井的水。一种解释是（作者推断）：这些例外比几十个典型病例更难用别的说法解释，比如“这一带空气不好”。
paras.en: What made this investigation persuasive was not the removal of the pump handle but the way the questions were asked: not merely what the dead had drunk, but what happened to those who did not drink it. The workhouse and the brewery stood close to the well and suffered almost nothing; the percussion-cap works and Mrs. E, one near and one far away, both drank from that well. One reading — the author's inference — is that these exceptions are harder to explain away than dozens of typical cases, such as bad air in the district.

paras.zh: 怀特黑德的转变同样要紧。他本以为调查会推翻水泵说，结果找到了一个比暴发早几天发病的病例，并促成了证实污物进井的检查。作者推断，一个抱着反对意见去查的人，查完改变看法，这样的结论往往比一群本来就同意的人互相印证更可信——前提是，他把自己的怀疑和查证过程都写了下来，供别人挑错。
paras.en: Whitehead's change of mind matters just as much. He expected his investigation to disprove the pump theory, and instead he found a case that began days before the outbreak and prompted the inquiry that showed how filth entered the well. The author's inference: when someone who begins in opposition tests a claim and ends up changing his mind, the result is often more convincing than a chorus of people who already agreed — provided he writes down both his doubts and his checking, so that others can pick them apart.

paras.zh: 证据也有边界。斯诺的饮水情况多是从别人那里打听来的，有问不到的，也可能有记错的；E太太那两例来自她儿子的转述。拆把手时疫情已在消退，所以不能说是拆把手终止了疫情；一种可能是，它挡住的是之后继续来喝这口井的人。女婴的污物与这次暴发之间，找到的是渗漏通道和时间上的吻合，不是化验报告。
paras.en: The evidence has boundaries. Most of Snow's information on who drank what came second-hand; some cases could not be asked about, and some may have been misremembered. The two deaths involving Mrs. E reached him through her son's account. When the handle was removed the outbreak was already fading, so one cannot say the removal ended it; one possibility is that it stopped people who came later from continuing to drink at that well. Between the infant's soiled napkins and this outbreak, what was found was a percolation route and a match in timing — not a laboratory report.

paras.zh: 假设你在一家做配送调度的小公司，连续三天傍晚订单大面积超时，人人都怀疑前天夜里那次发布。先别急着回滚：学斯诺先问一句，谁没事——那两个没超时的片区，是不是没走同一套调度服务？把没出事的人群列成清单，常常比盯着出事的那批人更快找到边界。
paras.en: Suppose you work at a small delivery-dispatch company, and for three evenings running a large share of orders arrive late. Everyone suspects a release that went out the night before the trouble began. Don't rush to roll it back. Do what Snow did and ask first who was fine: were the two districts that stayed on time running a different dispatch service? Drawing up a list of the unaffected cohorts often finds the boundary faster than staring at the people who were hit.

paras.zh: 复盘会上，一位原本想证明不是新流程之过的同事翻出更早的日志，发现了真正的触发点。把他的查证过程原样记下来，哪怕结论不讨喜；同时把结论分成已确认和机制推测两栏，别让一份整齐的叙述掩盖证据到底有多硬。
paras.en: At the postmortem, a colleague who wanted to prove the new workflow was not at fault digs through older logs and uncovers the real trigger. Record his investigation exactly as it happened, even if the conclusion is unwelcome; and split the findings into two columns — confirmed and inferred mechanism — so that a tidy narrative cannot blur how hard the evidence actually is.

paras.zh: 这是一次靠观察和打听的调查，没有对照实验；今天排查公共卫生问题有化验和更严格的流行病学方法，方法本身不必照搬。也别把它讲成孤胆英雄的故事：斯诺提出了问题，济贫委员会拆了把手，调查委员会和怀特黑德补上了关键证据，而委员会对水怎样致病始终没有下结论。
paras.en: This was an investigation built on observation and enquiry, with no controlled experiment. Public health investigations today have laboratory tests and stricter epidemiological methods, and the method itself need not be imitated. Nor should the episode be told as a lone-hero story: Snow raised the question, the Board of Guardians removed the handle, and the inquiry committee and Whitehead supplied the crucial evidence — while the Committee never concluded how the water caused the disease.

paras.zh: 作者提出一个反事实供参考：假如1851年或1853至54年的下水道深沟真的挖穿了古代瘟疫坑，当时的解释很可能滑向地下瘴气被扰动，水的说法会更难立足。实际的工程核查恰好帮这次调查排掉了这条岔路——排除一个像样的替代解释，本身就是证据的一部分。
paras.en: The author offers a counterfactual worth holding on to. Had the sewer cuttings of 1851 or 1853-54 actually passed through an ancient plague pit, the explanation of the day would most likely have slid toward disturbed miasma underground, and the water account would have been harder to sustain. The works records happened to clear this side road for the inquiry — and ruling out a respectable rival explanation is itself part of the evidence.

scenario.zh: 虚构情境：一家连锁烘焙坊的三家门店在同一个周末出现顾客腹泻投诉，公司初步怀疑一批奶油；A门店已停用该批次，之后仍有零星投诉。负责采购的质量经理最初想证明不是奶油的问题。
scenario.en: Fictional setting: a bakery chain sees customer complaints of diarrhoea at three stores over the same weekend, and the company initially suspects a batch of cream. Store A has already stopped using that batch, yet sporadic complaints continue. The quality manager in charge of procurement originally set out to prove the cream was not at fault.

question.zh: 在化验结果出来之前，你会依据什么证据停用这批奶油、通知顾客，还是保持沉默？停用的代价是销毁库存并承认风险，不停用的代价是可能继续有人受害——哪一种错误你觉得更难挽回？
question.en: Before the lab results arrive, what evidence would make you stop using this batch and notify customers — or stay silent? Stopping means destroying stock and conceding a risk; not stopping means people may keep being harmed. Which error do you think is harder to undo?

assumptions.zh: 假设投诉例数尚少、因果未确认，但该批次奶油确实覆盖三家门店；假设公开通知会触发监管上报流程。
assumptions.en: Assume the number of complaints is still small and causation is unconfirmed, but the cream batch did reach all three stores; and assume a public notice would trigger a regulatory reporting process.

steps.zh: 先列谁没事：未使用该批次的门店或产品线有无同类投诉；核对发病时间是否晚于批次到货时间；请一位不想要既定结论的同事独立复核订单与制作记录；设定临时下架的触发线，例如出现第二例与该批次相关的病例即停用。
steps.en: First list who was fine: do stores or product lines that did not use the batch show similar complaints? Check whether onset times fall after the batch was delivered. Ask a colleague who does not want the settled conclusion to review the orders and production records independently. Set a trigger for temporary withdrawal — for example, a second case linked to the batch means stop using it.

alternative.zh: 另一种合理选择是先只在A门店小范围停用并留样化验、暂不公开通知：理由是证据尚弱，避免错误归因和恐慌；代价是若判断错误会延误。
alternative.en: Another reasonable choice is to withdraw the batch only at store A on a small scale and keep samples for testing, without a public notice: the reasoning is that the evidence is still weak and one wants to avoid wrong attribution and panic; the cost is that if the judgement is wrong, action is delayed.

uncertainty_note.zh: 主要事实与数字出自斯诺1855年的著作及他提交调查委员会的报告；怀特黑德的转变、40号女婴和化粪池调查出自同一份委员会报告里他本人的记述与委员会的调查。两者是不同的来源基础，但并非完全独立：斯诺本人也是委员会成员。街区的瘟疫地旧事与下水道工程核查出自委员会报告；雷管厂一例出自斯诺的记述。饮水情况多为转述，有问不到的病例；E太太与侄女两例来自她儿子的转述。拆把手与疫情下降的因果无法确定。1854年没有细菌学说，“霍乱毒物”是斯诺当时的说法。本篇未取得中央卫生机构对此事的意见，因此不写其立场。
uncertainty_note.en: The principal facts and figures come from Snow's 1855 book and from the report he submitted to the inquiry committee. Whitehead's change of mind, the infant at No. 40 and the cesspool investigation come from his own account and the Committee's enquiry in the same committee report. The two rest on different source bases, but are not fully independent: Snow himself sat on the Committee. The neighbourhood's plague-field history and the sewer-works check come from the committee report; the percussion-cap manufactory case comes from Snow's own account. Information about who drank what is mostly hearsay, with cases that could not be asked about; the two deaths involving Mrs. E and her niece reach us through her son's account. Whether removing the handle caused the decline in cases cannot be determined. In 1854 there was no germ theory; "the cholera poison" was Snow's term of the time. No comment from a central health authority on this episode was obtained, so none is attributed.
